criteria.evidence: All four detailed-stage sections plus Agent intent are present and substantive, e.g. Benefit hypothesis 'How we will know: a capability with no domain, serving a confirmed business intent, is reported ready by the ready check; and Garura's own model ... passes the ontology check and the spine linter with no link that points at nothing.'; Boundary has In/Out/Never lines; Guiding rules has six rules; Functionalities lists fn-724, fn-597, fn-725, fn-726; ICE has every label.

'In: the ready rule — when a capability or functionality may be planned or built. It is the one gate that decides whether work can start, so it belongs with the links it reads.' and 'Never: let a missing domain block work. A missing domain is a warning for alignment, because the rule from Kapil (2026-10-21) is that nothing is blocked.' and 'Every link is checked by a script, not by judgment, so the same model always gives the same answer about what is ready and what is broken.'

Every section is a list of discrete bullets with a label or lead clause ('In:', 'Out:', 'Never:', 'Goal:', 'Limit:'); Functionalities are brief linked index lines stating behavior, e.g. 'A capability or functionality is ready without a domain (fn-724) — the ready check drops the domain and reads confirmed intents and open needs instead.' No user-story phrasing.

What: 'This capability is where "what links to what" is decided, so every play reads the same rules.' Why: 'Today that is blocked, because a node is not "ready" until it links all the way up to a domain (ADR 043), so no play may plan or build from it.' Edges: 'Out: building, viewing or changing plan files and their tracker issues — Build a plan (cap-718), View plans (cap-719) and Manage a plan (cap-720) own those.' and 'Never: change how model pages are saved'. Minor vocabulary gap (not failing): 'spine', 'spine linter' and 'ICE' are used without a one-clause gloss; adding e.g. 'the spine (the model's index file of nodes and their links)' would make a cold reader fully self-sufficient.
